verdict.rationale: WezTerm's configuration is a plain-text Lua file (.wezterm.lua in the home directory) that is watched and auto-reloaded, and the docs explicitly support carrying the config alongside the binary. Several independent users report syncing a single WezTerm config across Macs, Linux, Windows and WSL with chezmoi or nix/home-manager, calling it easy to diff and apply. Missing for 10: first-party documentation stating that every setting lives in the file, and documented alternative config paths such as XDG locations for dotfiles layouts.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can keep the terminal's full configuration as plain-text files in my dotfiles and sync it across machines

citations.quote: Create a file named `.wezterm.lua` in your home directory
wezterm will watch the config file that it loads; if/when it changes, the configuration will be automatically reloaded and the majority of options will take effect immediately.
to support users that carry their wezterm application and configuration around on a thumb drive, wezterm will look for the config file in the same location as wezterm.exe
With Wezterm it's just Lua code, easy to diff and easy to apply.
Keeps a single WezTerm config, wraps it in a nix expression for home-manager/NixOS, and symlinks it on Windows as a portal to WSL.
